findings.claim: The requirement that every multi-tile footprint be square contradicts the required rectangular boilers and steam engines.
findings.failure_scenario: A parser enforcing this rule and AC-2 rejects valid 3x2 boilers and 3x5 steam engines, preventing the phase-2 power build.

findings.claim: Rotation does not distinguish recipe keys from direction characters or reserve direction characters against use as recipe keys.
findings.failure_scenario: A permitted declaration such as '@v automation-science-pack' produces assembler tiles 'Av'; one implementation preserves the recipe during rotation while another rotates 'v' to '<', losing or changing the recipe.

findings.claim: The fingerprint of 'everything' has no defined fields or exclusions for ordinary simulation changes.
findings.failure_scenario: One implementation includes character positions, belt contents and machine progress, causing checks on a running factory to become stale immediately; another fingerprints only entity placement and misses recipe or configuration changes relevant to lint.

findings.claim: The fingerprint boundary does not cover all external power-network dependencies used by lint.
findings.failure_scenario: Power lint passes using a generator or connecting pole outside the tag's bounding box plus four tiles; that source is then removed, but build accepts the unchanged local fingerprint and constructs an unpowered layout.

findings.claim: Power lint bounds its scan geographically without defining traversal of ghost pole networks extending beyond that boundary.
findings.failure_scenario: A lab tag connects through a long, separately tagged ghost pole line to a planned steam engine; lint cannot see the distant source and reports no-power-source despite the complete planned connection.

findings.claim: The generic prove success conditions omit boilers, steam engines and labs despite requiring every layout to be proven working.
findings.failure_scenario: A tag containing a steam engine without steam or a lab without electricity returns success because none of its entities belong to the types whose status determines the exit code.

findings.claim: AC-21 requires a production-window test to pass using AC-12's instantaneous status conditions, which can reject a functioning production line.
findings.failure_scenario: The line produces and consumes red flasks during the 3600 ticks, but the gear assembler is temporarily waiting for ingredients at the final tick; prove fails even though the required research automation is operating.

findings.claim: Force-wide red-flask consumption does not establish that the newly built line supplied the research.
findings.failure_scenario: Existing labs consume previously stocked red flasks while the new line has a broken delivery connection; positive force consumption and locally acceptable entity statuses can satisfy AC-21 without any new flask reaching a lab.

findings.claim: The optional N argument to mine has neither a defined unit nor a default or stopping condition when omitted.
findings.failure_scenario: For 'mine X Y' on a large ore patch, one implementation mines once while another continues until the patch is exhausted or inventory fills, leaving the caller waiting through thousands of mining cycles.

findings.claim: The prohibition on changing existing saves is not reconciled with live tests that alter the user's hosted game.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer runs the required mining, building and research tests in the currently hosted save, and autosave persists those changes; another implementer requires a disposable copy, but the spec never establishes that prerequisite.
